portfolio.title: Portfolio
portfolio.subtitle: GIS research, tools, and projects I've built.

items.title: California Wildfire StoryMap
items.description: An interactive StoryMap on how California's wildfires have grown in size and number since 2000, where they concentrate, and how the state's official Fire Hazard Severity Zones compare against where fires have actually burned. Built around five maps (a county choropleth, a proportional symbol map, perimeters classed by size, a dissolved burn footprint, and the state hazard zones), working from statewide totals down to the record 2020 season.

image.caption: California Wildfires Since 2000, an ArcGIS StoryMap

items.title: Wildfire Structure Risk Tool
items.description: An ArcGIS Pro Python toolbox that scores individual structures as low, medium, or high wildfire risk from terrain and fuels. Slope is derived from a DEM, LANDFIRE fuel types are reclassified to hazard scores through a custom lookup, and each structure is rated on the worst fuel found inside California's 100-foot defensible space radius. Written in Python with arcpy and debugged against a study area in Idyllwild, a mountain town in the San Jacintos.

items.title: Temporal NDVI Study of Man-Made Forests
items.description: Term research poster on China's Great Green Wall afforestation program, tracking land use change, the health of the new forest, and shifting weather patterns across the Gobi Desert from 2000 to 2022. Custom R code processed 22 years of Landsat imagery into per-zone NDVI to quantify forest growth and health directly.

image.caption: Temporal NDVI Study - China's Great Green Wall Program

items.title: Santa Barbara Wildfire Analysis
items.description: Two Landsat studies of the Santa Barbara area. The first is a five-class supervised land cover classification (water, burn scar, urban, vegetation, rock and sparse vegetation) built in QGIS with the Semi-Automatic Classification Plugin, running from Lake Cachuma down to Carpinteria, with an accuracy assessment at 86.5% overall and a kappa of 0.83. The second tracks the 2008 Gap and 2009 Jesusita burn scars in R, pulling mean NDVI out of each perimeter from 2007 through 2011 and comparing it against an unburned control site to measure how fast each one came back.

items.title: California Condor and Great Gray Owl Habitat Lost to Wildfire
items.description: A decade-by-decade look at how much California Condor and Great Gray Owl habitat has burned. Classed the CAL FIRE historic perimeter record by decade back to 1898, then clipped it to each species' range as mapped by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife. Fire extent inside the owl's range grows decade over decade, and the last 40 years are by far the heaviest.

items.title: GPS Field Collection and Density Analysis, UCSB Campus Sign Inventory
items.description: Collected GPS waypoints in the field to inventory campus regulatory signage, feeding a merged class dataset of 151 classified sign locations. Converted the waypoints and track logs to features in ArcGIS Pro, then ran kernel density estimation across the forbidden, warning, and informational categories and set it against a Euclidean density surface for comparison.

items.title: Primal Chase
items.description: A browser-based survival game in vanilla JavaScript, no framework and no libraries. Play as a hunted predator managing heat, fatigue, thirst, and hunger across a day/night cycle while outrunning hunters that never stop.

items.title: ryan-little.com
items.description: This site. A 3D Earth lit from the real sun position for the current UTC time, live cloud imagery on a three-hour refresh, and a 9,000-star field. The satellites in orbit are the navigation, and there's a hidden shooting star minigame. Three.js and vanilla JS, no framework.

sites.title: Pyrogeography
sites.description: A wildfire publication. Each post covers one fire: the history, the terrain, and what the record actually says, with an original map built for the piece. In preparation, launching with the first fire.

sites.title: Summit Register
sites.description: Trail reports from Southern California and the Sierra: routes, conditions, GPS data, and what a peak is actually like to climb. In preparation, carrying over the reports currently published on ryanpdlittle.com.

items.title: PicSplitter
items.description: A Python command-line tool that splits large images into a configurable grid of tiles. Written for GIS workflows where imagery is too large to process in one piece in ArcGIS or QGIS.

about.title: About Me
about.subtitle: Geospatial analyst in San Diego. GIS production and quality control by day, wildfire mapping and Python tools the rest of the time.

headshot.caption: Big Bend National Park

sections.title: Background
content: Geography has been part of how I read the world since growing up in San Diego, with desert to the east, mountains to the north, and ocean to the west.

I studied it at UC Santa Barbara, earning a B.A. in Geography with an emphasis in Geographic Information Science and a 3.5 major GPA. Strongest coursework: a three-quarter remote sensing sequence, air photo interpretation through Landsat, LiDAR, and MODIS in QGIS, finishing in R, plus a course on optimization methods for network and location-allocation problems.

sections.title: Professional
content: Quality control geospatial analyst at CACI, supporting a federal geospatial data program, remote from San Diego.

I run feature-level QC and validation on transportation, hydrography, structures, land cover, and geonames data in ArcGIS Pro, checking it against contract accuracy and attribution standards before it ships. I also give structured technical feedback and training to 20+ technicians, and run a recurring Q&A and mentorship group on ArcGIS Pro workflows and spec interpretation.

image.caption: Remote sensing analysis, water feature mapping in Greenland

sections.title: Currently Studying
content: Working toward a Graduate Certificate in Spatial Data Science at Penn State, through the World Campus while working full time.
Coursework so far has covered GIS programming and automation with Python and arcpy, and cartography and visualization. Both produced the wildfire projects in my portfolio.
All fifteen credits carry into Penn State's M.S. in Spatial Data Science, which I plan to start once the certificate confers.

sections.title: Skills
content: Languages: Python, R, SQL, JavaScript, HTML & CSS
GIS Tools: ArcGIS Pro, ArcMap, ArcGIS Online, ArcGIS StoryMaps, QGIS
Specializations: Remote Sensing, Spatial Analysis, Spatial Databases, Data Visualization, Quality Control

sections.title: Outside of Work
content: Hiker and traveler, 12 countries and counting, with a strong preference for national parks and places that take some effort to reach.
Also into soccer, building computers, server tinkering, and web development.
Open to geospatial analyst opportunities. Reach out via LinkedIn or email.
